goal: A scheduling pass built from a task set containing one structurally-invalid task (duplicate id, self-dependency, or cycle member) excludes that task with a recorded reason and still schedules the remaining valid, independent tasks.

relevant: packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_work_graph.py -- WorkGraph.__init__ raises WorkGraphValidationError on a duplicate id (~line 135), self-dependency (~line 151), and cycle (~line 169), poisoning every unrelated task in the pass. Missing prerequisites are already recorded as non-raising GraphValidationIssue on .issues -- extend that contain-and-record posture to these three structural defects: isolate the offending task(s) with a recorded reason and build the graph from the survivors
non_goals: Do not modify files under any tests/ directory except to ADD the new packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_workgraph_isolate_invalid_task.py; do not weaken or delete existing assertions
Do not silently drop an invalid task with no recorded reason -- the exclusion reason must name the offender
Do not change the orchestrate main-loop containment (that is its own task that consumes this one)
Do not read or write under .flywheel/verification/
constraints: The exclusion reason is recorded (e.g. as a GraphValidationIssue-style record or equivalent) and names the offending task id(s) -- recoverable, not lost
Valid, independent tasks in the same set remain schedulable (present in the ready/selectable set)
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done
edge_cases: Duplicate id, self-dependency, and cycle-member are each isolated; a valid independent task in the same set stays selectable -- dropping the whole pass must fail the test
BOTH halves are asserted: valid tasks survive AND the exclusion is recorded with a reason naming the offender; a silent drop must fail
